newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland may revise currency law in 1998 - c.bank. [CORRECTED 14:20 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Poland may revise currency law in 1998 - c.bank. [CORRECTED 14:20 GMT]

text.p: Poland may next year revise its currency law, allowing current account trade transactions in zlotys, to bring the currency closer to full convertibility, a deputy-president of the central bank said.

"I hope that from 1998 the currency law will be changed so that the zloty can be a currency in which (current account) foreign trade transactions can be made," Krzysztof Barburski told a financial forum on exchange rate risks on Thursday.

Presently the zloty is fully convertible domestically but cannot be used as the settlement currency in foreign trade transactions outside of the Polish banking system (corrects to make clear that it is outside the Polish banking system that the zloty cannot be used as a settlement currency).
